references.text: Moses' first meeting with God on the mountain, where God reveals Himself in the burning bush, a precursor to the revelation at Sinai
The Lord calls Moses up the mountain to receive the tablets of the law, a continuation of God's revelation at Sinai
Moses goes up again to Mount Sinai by the Lord's command to receive the new tablets of the law
Moses recalls that the Lord came from Sinai and rose from the mountain peak for His people
The psalm describes how the earth shook and the heavens dripped at God's presence on Sinai
The Lord came from Sinai to the sanctuary, a reference to God's descent upon the mountain
Nehemiah recalls that God descended on Mount Sinai and spoke to the people from heaven
Stephen refers to Moses who was on Mount Sinai and received living words to give to the Israelites
Paul uses Mount Sinai as an image of the old covenant and the law given there
The letter to the Hebrews contrasts the revelation at Sinai with the revelation of the new covenant, describing a mountain that could be touched and burned with fire
Narrative parallel: Both verses illustrate Moses' obedient ascent up Sinai following God's direct call, underscoring his role as mediator in various stages of covenant history.

Direct narrative continuation: The calling in the source verse leads directly to verse 34's description of the Lord's glory resting on the mountain and the cloud covering it before the final conversation.
Narrative connection: Describes the immediate consequence of Moses' ascent in the source verse, where the cloud covers the mountain and marks God's holy presence.
Thematic parallel: Both verses highlight God's active call to Moses that presupposes his response ('Here I am' / 'Moses went up'), marking the start of new important phases in salvation history.
